title: Synonymous Sentences
description:
You are given a list of equivalent string pairs `synonyms` where `synonyms[i] = [si, ti]` indicates that `si` and `ti` are equivalent strings. You are also given a sentence `text`.

Return *all possible synonymous sentences **sorted lexicographically***.

examples.input: synonyms = [["happy","joy"],["sad","sorrow"],["joy","cheerful"]], text = "I am happy today but was sad yesterday"
examples.output: ["I am cheerful today but was sad yesterday","I am cheerful today but was sorrow yesterday","I am happy today but was sad yesterday","I am happy today but was sorrow yesterday","I am joy today but was sad yesterday","I am joy today but was sorrow yesterday"]

examples.input: synonyms = [["happy","joy"],["cheerful","glad"]], text = "I am happy today but was sad yesterday"
examples.output: ["I am happy today but was sad yesterday","I am joy today but was sad yesterday"]

constraints: text consists of at most 10 words.
All the pairs of synonyms are unique.
The words of text are separated by single spaces.

testcases.input: [["happy","joy"],["sad","sorrow"],["joy","cheerful"]], text = "I am happy today but was sad yesterday"
testcases.expected: ["I am cheerful today but was sad yesterday","I am cheerful today but was sorrow yesterday","I am happy today but was sad yesterday","I am happy today but was sorrow yesterday","I am joy today but was sad yesterday","I am joy today but was sorrow yesterday"]

testcases.input: [["happy","joy"],["cheerful","glad"]], text = "I am happy today but was sad yesterday"
testcases.expected: ["I am happy today but was sad yesterday","I am joy today but was sad yesterday"]

hints: Analyze the constraints and data structures appropriate for Synonymous Sentences.
Formulate an optimal state transition or traversal invariant.
Consider corner testcases and boundary limits.
